transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon, thank you for calling S-Net Mobile Technical Support. My name is Benjamin speaking today. How can I help you?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Benjamin, my name is Tadhg O'Sullivan. I'm calling because my mobile keeps dropping from 4G directly to 'No Service' halfway through calls whenever I'm inside my house.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, I am really sorry to hear you are dealing with dropped calls indoors, sir. I completely understand how frustrating and disruptive that is when you rely on your phone at home.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It really is, especially because I use my Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra for client consultations from my home study, and three calls have cut out today alone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I appreciate how stressful that must be during client consultations, and I will do everything I can to help get this investigated for you. First, could you confirm your billing address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Sure, my billing address is 28 Crescent Gardens, Bath, BA1 2NA, and my four-digit security PIN is 6042.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you very much, I have verified your billing address at 28 Crescent Gardens and your PIN 6042 on the system now. Let me pull up the S-Net radio mast map for BA1 2NA.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: When I check the coverage status page on your website, it claims the outdoor mast near Royal Victoria Park is working normally, which makes no sense.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at the cell site dashboard for BA1 2NA, the primary macro mast is site SN-BATH-09, which is approximately six hundred metres west of Crescent Gardens.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, and if I walk out into my front garden on the street, my Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra gets three or four bars of 4G and holds a call fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, site SN-BATH-09 shows green operational status across both its 1800 megahertz and 800 megahertz 4G LTE carriers right now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then why does the signal collapse completely to 'No Service' with an exclamation mark the moment I answer or place a voice call inside my living room or study?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bath has a lot of thick Georgian Bath stone walls, which can attenuate higher-frequency radio waves quite heavily as they travel indoors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I've lived in this same Georgian terrace for four years on S-Net Mobile, Benjamin, and my indoor calls never cut out like this until last Tuesday!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I hear you, sir, and I am genuinely sorry that this sudden change since last Tuesday has been interrupting your workday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did S-Net change something on the mast last week, or is my phone failing to hand over between frequencies when a voice call starts?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me look at the recent engineering change log for the Bath cluster of cell sites to see if any maintenance took place last Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Are you still there, Benjamin? The line went completely silent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, yes, I am still here, sir, my screen was just taking a while to load the regional cell site maintenance log for Somerset and Bath.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, well I thought the call had dropped on your end too for a second! What did the maintenance log show?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It shows that on Monday the ninth of October, the radio optimization team adjusted the antenna tilt angle on sector two of mast SN-BATH-09 by two degrees.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait—they tilted the antenna on the mast right before my indoor calls started failing on Tuesday?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They performed a routine traffic-balancing tilt adjustment because of high daytime congestion near the city centre shopping district.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So by tilting the antenna toward the shopping centre, have they weakened the indoor signal reaching Crescent Gardens?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is possible that the indoor RSRP signal strength on the 1800 megahertz band dipped just below the handover threshold inside your ground-floor rooms.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And when a 4G VoLTE voice call starts, instead of staying connected, the phone just drops straight to zero bars and says 'Call Failed'!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how exasperating it is when a business call drops mid-sentence, sir, and you have been very patient while we look into this.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Isn't there anything we can check or configure on my end right now so I can actually take my afternoon client calls indoors?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Honestly, the radio parameters are controlled from the network side at the base station controller, so I mainly need to log the signal drop timestamps from your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you see the dropped call records on my network call trace from this morning?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open the core network IMS call signalling trace for your mobile number ending in 4491 to view today's call release causes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There should be three dropped calls between nine thirty and eleven fifteen this morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I see one call at 09:34 that lasted two minutes and twelve seconds before terminating with radio link failure code RLF-408.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That was my first client of the morning! Right in the middle of reviewing a contract.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And I see a second call at 10:18 lasting forty-seven seconds, and a third at 11:09 lasting one minute and fifty seconds, both ending with RLF-408 on sector two.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Every single one of those showed two bars of 4G before I dialled, and then ten seconds into speaking the bars vanished completely.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That happens when the dedicated voice bearer stays locked onto a weak high-band carrier rather than stepping down cleanly to the 800 megahertz indoor layer.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why wouldn't it step down cleanly to the 800 megahertz indoor layer like it used to do before last Tuesday?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When they adjusted the antenna tilt on SN-BATH-09, the neighbour-cell handover offset table may not have been recalibrated for indoor edge users on Crescent Gardens.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Let me check if there are any other settings or anything else on my account profile while you're looking at the signalling trace.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sure, let me open the provisioning tab on your mobile profile now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Anyone there? Benjamin, have you gone quiet again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, I am still on the line, sir, I was just reading through the provisioning parameters on the second monitor here.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You really ought to tell me before going silent for nearly a minute, I kept thinking my phone had cut out again!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am very sorry about that silence, sir, I didn't mean to leave you wondering if the line had dropped.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, well what did you see on the provisioning tab?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your voice provisioning profile shows standard 4G VoLTE active on the core IMS switch with no bars or restrictions on the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, so what do you need to put into the engineering ticket for the radio team?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am filling out the radio access network propagation form right now. By the way, what make and model of phone are you using?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you right at the beginning of the call—it's a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra! I mentioned it twice when we started speaking.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Oh, my apologies, sir, I completely missed writing that down earlier—a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra, let me enter that in the device field now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, a Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra bought directly from S-Net last year.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, I have entered Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra onto the radio investigation form along with the three RLF-408 failure timestamps from this morning.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there anything we should test on the phone itself right now—like toggling a setting or checking an alternative connection method—so I can survive the next few days?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To be completely honest with you, sir, since the RLF-408 code comes from the sector two antenna tilt on SN-BATH-09, changing things on the phone won't alter the mast beam.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you don't want me to check any network mode menus or anything in my Samsung settings at all?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, there's no need to go digging through your phone menus today, because our radio engineers have to review the tilt angle on the mast side.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, how does the mast investigation actually get handled from here? I don't want this ticket just sitting at the bottom of a queue.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am taking personal ownership of this case for you, sir. I have raised priority radio propagation ticket RAN-662019-BA directly with our South West RF engineering team.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What will the South West RF engineering team actually do with ticket RAN-662019-BA?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have attached your three IMS call drop traces from 09:34, 10:18, and 11:09 and requested a remote electrical downtilt rollback and inter-band handover audit on SN-BATH-09.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can they adjust that electrical tilt remotely from their operations centre, or do they have to send a rigger up the mast in Royal Victoria Park?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The remote electrical tilt and the 1800-to-800 megahertz handover threshold can both be adjusted remotely from the Bristol network operations centre.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And how long will it take them to run that audit and adjust the mast?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The service-level turnaround for a Tier 3 RF propagation and tilt recalibration is up to five working days, though I have marked your ticket urgent for home-working impact.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Five working days is a long time to have my indoor calls dropping every couple of minutes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how inconvenient that five-day window is when you have clients ringing you, sir, which is why I am also applying a fifteen-pound goodwill credit to your next bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you for the fifteen-pound credit, Benjamin, I appreciate the gesture even if it doesn't keep my calls connected today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have already posted that fifteen-pound credit onto your mobile account, and I have scheduled a personal callback from me to you on Friday afternoon at four o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will you text me the ticket number and the Friday callback details in case the voice call cuts out when you ring me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Absolutely, I have just sent an SMS to your mobile with reference RAN-662019-BA, the fifteen-pound credit confirmation, and my Friday 16:00 follow-up slot.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My phone just buzzed on the desk with the text message, so SMS messages are still coming through indoors even when voice calls fail.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, SMS uses the lightweight control channel rather than a continuous VoLTE voice bearer, so text updates will reach you reliably inside your study.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All right, well I suppose for the rest of this week I will have to stand out in the front garden with my coat on whenever a client rings me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I really am sorry you have to step outside into the garden for your calls in the meantime, sir, and I will push the Bristol RF engineers for an early review.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, let's hope they roll back that antenna change before Friday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will monitor ticket RAN-662019-BA daily in my own worklist and text you the moment the Bristol RF team updates the handover parameters on SN-BATH-09.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, so for now the indoor call drops are still happening until the mast team makes that change.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is correct, sir, the indoor signal drops remain open pending the RF engineering adjustments over the next few days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, I'll look out for your text or call on Friday afternoon at four o'clock.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else I can check for you today while we are on the line, sir?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, that's all for now, thank you Benjamin.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, sir, and please complete the brief survey after this call. Have a good rest of your afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
